chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat from the top of the tharid (bread and meat stew), and eat from its sides, for the blessing is in its top.'

key_terms.الثَّرِيد: A traditional dish of bread soaked in meat broth/stew
key_terms.رَأْس: Top or head (referring to the top layer of the dish)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for eating tharid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) regarding the etiquette of eating tharid, advising against consuming the top layer first and instead instructing to eat from the sides, as the blessing (barakah) resides in the top. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on preserving divine favor through mindful consumption, illustrating how physical habits can serve as vessels for spiritual abundance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Do not eat from the top of Al-Sareyd (a porridge), and eat from its side, for the fennel-flower seeds are in its top’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ’
Do not eat from the top of Tharid but eat from its sides because blessing is on its top.’” (Tharid is loaf of bread broken in pieces in broth.)
